description.para: Strongly-typed wrappers for converting dynamic values and expressions to specific types recognised by µTest++ comparators.

These type aliases provide a type-safe mechanism for explicitly converting values to the required types for µTest++ test expressions and comparators. Each alias is a wrapper around detail::value<T>, ensuring that the value is treated as the specified type within the framework.
The to_* forms replaced the older _i, _u8, etc. aliases, which were deprecated in version 3.2.0.

simplesect.title: Deprecated
simplesect.para: Pass the plain values to the function comparators eq(), ne(), gt(), ge(), lt(), and le() instead; they report the operands in the same way. For the floating-point values compared with a tolerance, use approx() (since 6.0.0).

description.para: The v5.0.1 names of the to_* type wrappers.

The Boost UT style names, with a leading underscore, kept for compatibility with the existing applications. Each one is an alias of the corresponding to_* wrapper, so the wrapped values are compared and reported in the same way. They do not conflict with the literal operators with the same suffixes (42_i), which are in the literals namespace.
GCC reports the deprecation only when the alias names the type of a declaration, not when it is used in an expression, as in _i (expr); Clang reports it in both cases.

simplesect.title: Deprecated
simplesect.para: Pass the plain values to the function comparators eq(), ne(), gt(), ge(), lt(), and le() instead; the to_* type wrappers that replaced these aliases (since 3.2.0) are deprecated too (since 6.0.0).

detaileddescription.para: Colours are used when stdout is a terminal; on the platforms without isatty(), such as the embedded ones, they are not used.
Colours are always used, for example in the CI systems that render the ANSI escape sequences but do not provide a terminal, or on embedded targets whose output is displayed by a terminal.
Colours are never used.

briefdescription.para: The use of colours in the console output.

detaileddescription.para: Selected with the --colour command-line option (or its American spelling --color, or its alternative --use-colour, also spelled --use-color), or with runner_options::colour; the default is automatic. The names follow the values of --color in the GNU tools.
Only the human-readable reporter uses colours; the TAP reporter never does, since the ANSI escape sequences are not part of the TAP syntax. The output file never receives colours, whatever the mode.
The TAP reporter, compliant with TAP version 14.
The human-readable reporter, with optional colours.
Selected with the --reporter command-line option, or with runner_options::selected_reporter; the default is tap.
No console output; only the exit code is returned.
Displays only the failed checks and the overall session summary; the TAP reporter also displays one result line per test suite, counted by the plan, and the failed checks as comments.
Displays test suite and test case results; the individual checks are shown only for failures, the passed checks being counted, and, in the TAP blocks, numbered by bare ok lines.
Displays all results, including passed checks, for maximum detail.

briefdescription.para: The verbosity levels for test reporting.

detaileddescription.para: The level is selected with the --silent, --quiet, and --verbose command-line options, or with runner_options::verbosity_level; the default is normal. The console output is intended for the people who watch the tests run, while the optional output file is intended for the integration with other tools. The level affects only the console output; the output file always receives the full report.

The quiet level displays the failed checks, with the names of the suite and of the test cases that contain them, and the totals; the passed checks and the passed test cases are not displayed. To also see them, use the verbose level, or keep quiet and use an output file, which receives them.

briefdescription.para: Primary namespace for the µTest++ testing framework.

detaileddescription.para: The micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus namespace encapsulates all core components, types, and utilities of the µTest++ testing framework, providing a dedicated scope for its public API.

The main classes (the runners, and the suites and test cases) are defined directly in this namespace. Several nested namespaces group specific aspects of the framework: math (mathematical utilities), extension (the concepts for custom comparators, operators, and helpers), reflection (source locations and type names), literals (user-defined literals), operators (comparison and logical operators), utility (utility functions), and detail (internal implementation details, including the reporters and the value wrappers).
The declarations are in the headers of the include/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus folder, and the non-inline definitions in the src folder.
